Name of Institution: The Ministry of Mines and Steels Development (MMSD)
Mandate:
Formulate and implement national policies for solid minerals development, regulate and supervise the mining sector,
 and drive investment and value addition.
Value Chain Role: Policy leadership, regulation and strategic coordination across the mineral value chain.
Functions: Sets policy and legal framework for mining; oversees regulatory agencies; coordinates reforms, federal–state relations and international cooperation in the minerals sector.

Mandate: Administer and manage mineral titles in Nigeria through a transparent mining cadastre system.
Value Chain Role: Administration of mineral rights, licensing and tenure management.
Functions: Processes applications for exploration and mining licences; maintains the digital cadastre; grants, renews and revokes titles; and provides tenure information to government and investors.

Mandate: Enforce mine health, safety and technical standards and monitor compliance with mining regulations.
Value Chain Role: Operational oversight, safety enforcement and production monitoring.
Jurisdiction: All licensed mine sites in Nigeria
Functions: Inspects mine sites; investigates accidents and unsafe practices; verifies production data; and issues compliance directives and sanctions where necessary.

Mandate: Generate, store and disseminate geoscientific and mineral resource data for Nigeria.
Value Chain Role: Upstream geological mapping, resource identification and exploration support.
Jurisdiction: Entire national territory and offshore areas under Nigerian control
Functions: Carries out geological, geochemical and geophysical surveys; produces maps and reports; identifies mineral targets; and provides geodata to government, investors and researchers.

Name of Institution: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA)
Mandate: Enforce environmental laws, regulations and standards (excluding upstream oil and gas) across Nigeria.
Value Chain Role: Environmental compliance, pollution control and enforcement in mining and processing.
Jurisdiction: Federal Republic of Nigeria (excluding upstream petroleum operations)
Functions: Monitors environmental performance of facilities; enforces EIAs and sector regulations; investigates complaints and imposes sanctions for non‑compliance in mining and related activities.

Name of Institution: Raw Materials Research and Development Council (RMRDC)
Mandate: Promote research, development and utilisation of Nigeria’s raw materials for industrialisation.
Value Chain Role: Linking minerals to industry, processing and manufacturing value chains.
Jurisdiction: Nationwide raw materials and industrial sectors
Functions: Conducts studies on industrial raw materials; advises government and industry on local sourcing; supports projects that upgrade and substitute imported raw materials using Nigerian minerals.

Mandate: Promote transparency and accountability in the management of revenues from Nigeria’s extractive industries.
Value Chain Role: Revenue transparency, governance and accountability across the value chain.
Jurisdiction: All extractive sectors and government entities handling extractive revenues in Nigeria
Functions: Produces independent reconciliation reports; discloses payments and revenues; engages government, companies and civil society to strengthen governance of the minerals sector.

Name of Institution: The Department of Mines Environmental Compliance (MEC)
Mandate: Oversee and coordinate environmental compliance obligations specific to mining operations under MMSD.
Value Chain Role: Sector‑specific environmental oversight within the mining value chain.
Jurisdiction: Mining and quarrying operations across Nigeria
State/City: Abuja (with field presence through mines offices)
Functions: Reviews and monitors mine environmental management plans; works with NESREA and state authorities on remediation, closure and reclamation issues.

Mandate: Formalise, support and regulate artisanal and small‑scale mining activities in Nigeria.
Value Chain Role: ASM formalisation, support services and integration into the formal minerals economy.
Jurisdiction: Artisanal and small‑scale mining operators nationwide
State/City: Abuja (with outreach through state and zonal offices)
Functions: Supports cooperatives and licensing of ASM; provides extension and technical assistance; and promotes safer, more environmentally responsible practices among small‑scale miners.

Mandate: Provide financing and catalytic investments to stimulate exploration and development of Nigeria’s solid minerals.
Value Chain Role: Project finance, de‑risking exploration and supporting early‑stage development.
Jurisdiction: Eligible solid minerals projects across Nigeria
Functions: Invests in geoscience data, exploration and strategic projects; partners with private investors; and supports projects that enhance Nigeria’s mineral value addition.

Name of Institution: National Assembly Committee on Mines & Steel
Mandate: Exercise legislative oversight over the mines and steel sector and review relevant laws and budgets.
Value Chain Role: Legislative oversight, law‑making and budget scrutiny for the minerals sector.
Jurisdiction: Federal legislative oversight across all mining institutions and programmes
Functions: Reviews and amends mining and minerals laws; oversees MMSD and its agencies; and approves sectoral budgets and key policy instruments.

Name of Institution: National Steel Raw Materials Exploration Agency (NSRMEA )
Mandate: Explore and evaluate raw materials required for the iron and steel industry in Nigeria.
Value Chain Role: Upstream exploration for steel‑related minerals (iron ore, coal, limestone, etc.).
Jurisdiction: Prospective iron and steel raw material provinces across Nigeria
Functions: Carries out geological exploration and evaluation of iron ore, coal and other inputs; supports planning and development of the domestic steel industry.
